title: Fix sticky A/B assignment on retries + streaming reconnects
author: Jordan Lee
body: Summary: Fixes a bug where the route-level A/B experiment variant could flip across client retries and streaming reconnects. Root cause was that our assignment seed fell back to per-attempt request_id when the preferred sticky inputs (idempotency key / client request id / user sticky header) were absent, so each retry produced a different hash and could land in a different bucket. This PR introduces a stable retry/reconnect seed derived from the first attempt and propagated through gateway retry plumbing, plus a regression test covering both non-streaming retries and SSE reconnect. Context: Reported by Support (SUP-3928) and reproduced internally during dogfood when clients retried on 5xx/timeout or reconnected to streams after a disconnect; variant assignment changed while the experiment config remained the same, which breaks measurement assumptions and causes confusing user experience. What changed: 1) Gateway now computes a sticky assignment key in a deterministic precedence order: (a) x-redwood-sticky-key (explicit), else (b) x-redwood-idempotency-key, else (c) x-redwood-client-request-id, else (d) retry_token (new; set on first attempt and replayed on subsequent attempts/reconnects), else (e) request_id (last resort). 2) Added a small internal header between gateway layers: x-rw-ab-retry-token. For first attempts, we mint this token once per request and store it in the request context; for retries triggered by the gateway’s retry policy and for streaming reconnect handling, we re-use the same token so the assignment hash remains stable. 3) Streaming: for SSE reconnects (where the client may reconnect with Last-Event-ID / stream cursor), we now map the reconnect to the original stream session id and feed that into the same x-rw-ab-retry-token path. This keeps variant stable for the lifetime of the stream session. 4) Tests: Added regression tests to ensure that (a) a request retried twice with different request_id values yields the same variant and (b) an SSE reconnect for the same stream session yields the same variant. Files/areas: - gateway/middleware/ab_assignment.go: stabilize seed selection + propagate x-rw-ab-retry-token - gateway/middleware/streaming_reconnect.go: plumb stream session id into retry token path - pkg/abassign/sticky_key.go: centralized precedence + validation (length/charset) - gateway/middleware/ab_assignment_test.go: new regression test cases - pkg/abassign/sticky_key_test.go: unit tests for precedence rules and fallbacks Notes/guardrails: - This does not change the exposure event schema; it only ensures that variant is consistent given the same effective sticky key. Exposures are still emitted per attempt today (attempt counter already exists in the gateway context), which is desirable for debugging retries; metric aggregation remains based on experiment_id+variant. - Privacy: x-rw-ab-retry-token is an opaque random token (base64url) minted by the gateway, not derived from user identifiers. It is not logged at info level and is excluded from structured request logs via the header allowlist. - Backwards compatibility: If clients already send x-redwood-idempotency-key or x-redwood-client-request-id, behavior is unchanged except that retries now remain stable even if request_id changes. Example snippet (gateway/middleware/ab_assignment.go): "seed := abassign.StickySeed{Explicit: hdr("x-redwood-sticky-key"), IdempotencyKey: hdr("x-redwood-idempotency-key"), ClientRequestID: hdr("x-redwood-client-request-id"), RetryToken: ctx.Value(rwctx.ABRetryToken), RequestID: ctx.Value(rwctx.RequestID)}; key := abassign.SelectStickyKey(seed)" CI: - build (linux_amd64): pass - unit tests: pass - lint (golangci-lint): pass - integration (gateway): pass Review conversation: Vikram Singh: "Can we confirm the retry token won’t leak into logs/metrics? Also, does this impact exposure duplication?" Jordan Lee (author): "Yep—added it to the header denylist and verified it’s not included in the exposure tags allowlist. Exposures are still per attempt; this PR only stabilizes variant assignment so attempts don’t land in different variants." Mina Haddad: "What happens for clients that do their own retries (not gateway retries)?" Jordan Lee: "If they provide idempotency or client_request_id, stable. If they provide neither, behavior is still per-attempt (request_id) unless it’s a stream reconnect (where we can map to stream session). We’ll follow up in docs recommending idempotency for stable experiments." Ravi Menon: "Please add a unit test for precedence when explicit sticky key is present." Jordan Lee: "Added in pkg/abassign/sticky_key_test.go (explicit overrides idempotency/client IDs)." Allison Grant: "Any change to metric cardinality?" Jordan Lee: "No new dimensions; token not exported. Only changes internal seed selection." Merge: Squash merged to main. Release note: Fixes experiment variant stickiness across retries/stream reconnects to prevent variant flipping during A/B tests.
